items.title: 4 Reasons American Express Stock Is Having Its Worst Year Since 2015 Despite Record Earnings
items.summary: American Express stock is down 15.3% year-to-date despite posting record earnings and raising full-year guidance, marking its worst year since 2015. The decline is attributed to valuation pullback after a decade-long surge, declining gross margins due to increased customer reward expenses, concerns about consumer spending weakness amid economic headwinds, and uncertainty around AI investment costs. However, the stock trades at a cheap 17.8x earnings multiple, presenting a potential buying opportunity for long-term investors given the company's strong fundamentals and unique positioning in agentic commerce.

items.summary: Crown Castle (CCI) reported Q3 2026 AFFO per share of $1.24, up 10.7% YoY and beating estimates by 3.3%, benefiting from lower interest costs. However, revenues fell 7.2% to $995 million due to DISH terminations and Sprint cancellations impacting site rentals. The company raised its 2026 AFFO and EBITDA guidance, with AFFO now expected between $1.955-$2.005 billion.

items.title: UNP Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Volume Growth, Pricing Gains
items.summary: Union Pacific (UNP) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.53 per share, beating consensus by 1.7%, with revenues rising 15.3% to $7.20 billion. Freight revenues grew 14.9% driven by higher carloads and pricing gains, though fuel expenses surged 68.8%. The company maintains high-single-digit EPS growth outlook for 2026. Other transportation companies showed mixed results: Alaska Air Group beat earnings estimates but faced fuel headwinds, Wabtec beat earnings but missed revenue targets, and J.B. Hunt exceeded both earnings and revenue expectations.

items.title: Globe Life Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Weak Underwriting Income
items.summary: Globe Life reported Q3 2026 operating EPS of $4.84, slightly missing estimates but growing 0.6% year-over-year. Premium revenues rose 6.5%, but underwriting income fell 4.2% and expenses surged 11.5%, pressuring profitability. The company revised its 2026 EPS guidance downward to $15.35-$15.65 due to adverse results at United American, while raising share repurchase forecasts. Book value per share increased 22.8% year-over-year.

items.title: Prediction: Sandisk Stock Will Soar After Oct. 29. Here Are 379 Billion Reasons Why
items.summary: Sandisk stock has declined 32% since July despite strong fundamentals, as investors worry about AI infrastructure sustainability. However, the article argues the selloff is unjustified given robust NAND flash demand, expected 357% revenue growth in fiscal Q1, and a $379 billion addressable market opportunity in 2027. With the stock trading at just 8x forward earnings versus the S&P 500's 19x multiple, the author expects stronger-than-expected results on Oct. 29 could trigger a significant rally.

items.title: ROL's Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Weak Demand & Higher Costs
items.summary: Rollins, Inc. reported disappointing Q3 2026 results with earnings declining 2.9% year-over-year to 34 cents per share, missing consensus estimates. While revenues grew 6.2% to $1.09 billion, operating margins contracted 140 basis points to 20.5% due to rising costs and weak residential customer acquisition. Commercial and termite operations provided growth, but profitability suffered. The company is restructuring its marketing strategy and generated strong free cash flow of $235.5 million, up 28.8% year-over-year.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Innventure, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. and its officers for alleged securities fraud. The complaint alleges that the company made false statements about its subsidiary Accelsius's transformative deal with DarkNX, which allegedly lacked evidence of feasibility, and that revenue and cash targets for 2026 were not reasonably plausible. Investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 may be eligible to join the case.

items.title: LUV Q3 Earnings Beat on Record Revenues and Higher Fares
items.summary: Southwest Airlines (LUV) delivered exceptional Q3 2026 results with adjusted EPS surging 500% to 66 cents, beating estimates by 8.2%, and record revenues reaching $8.42 billion. Strong pricing power drove a 26.9% jump in average fares, though passenger volumes declined 3.2%. Despite a 61.7% surge in fuel costs, the airline expanded operating margins to 5.4%. The company provided Q4 guidance of 55-80 cents EPS and full-year 2026 guidance of $2.60-$2.85 EPS.

items.title: HON Q3 Earnings Beat on Automation Strength, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Honeywell Technologies (HON) reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.27, beating estimates of $2.17, with 34% year-over-year growth. Organic sales grew 7% across all segments. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.40-$8.45 and free cash flow expectations to $2.1 billion, driven by strength in building automation, industrial measurement, and process automation projects.

items.title: ROP Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Solid Organic Growth
items.summary: Roper Technologies reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $5.89, beating estimates by 1.7% with 15% year-over-year growth. Organic revenues grew 7%, driven by strong performance across all three segments, particularly Technology Enabled Products which grew 10%. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $22.35-$22.40 and expects revenue growth above 8%.

items.title: ALLE Q3 Earnings Beat on Americas Strength, Outlook Raised
items.summary: Allegion plc (ALLE) reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $2.60 per share, up 13% YoY and beating estimates by 4.4%, with revenues growing 9.6% to $1.17 billion. The Americas segment drove growth with 11.7% revenue increase on strong non-residential demand. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $9.05-$9.10 and revenue growth outlook to 9.5-10.5%, reflecting confidence in continued momentum.

items.title: AMG or BLK: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: In a value investor comparison, Affiliated Managers Group (AMG) emerges as the more attractive option compared to BlackRock (BLK). AMG holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook, a lower forward P/E of 10.68 versus BLK's 20.00, and a superior PEG ratio of 0.50 compared to BLK's 1.20. AMG also has a better Value grade of B versus BLK's F grade.

items.title: BGC vs. EVR: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
items.summary: A comparison of two Financial-Investment Bank sector stocks reveals BGC Group as the superior value opportunity. BGC holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 8.30 and PEG ratio of 0.42, while Evercore carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) with a forward P/E of 13.86 and PEG ratio of 1.14. BGC's improving earnings outlook and stronger valuation metrics make it the preferred choice for value investors.

items.title: United Rentals Tops Q3 Earnings & Revenue Estimates, Raises 2026 View
items.summary: United Rentals (URI) delivered robust third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted EPS surging 32.9% to $15.55 and revenues rising 15.7% to $4.89 billion, both beating consensus estimates. The specialty rental segment led growth with a 34.7% revenue jump and 250 bps margin expansion. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $18-$18.2 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $8.3-$8.4 billion, citing strong customer confidence and large-project momentum.

items.title: Lockheed Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Sales Increase Year Over Year
items.summary: Lockheed Martin reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $7.97, beating consensus estimates by 6.4%, with sales climbing 11.3% to $20.71 billion. The company's backlog surged to $291.98 billion, driven by strong performance in Missiles and Fire Control (up 24% YoY). LMT raised its 2026 full-year sales guidance to $80-$82 billion and adjusted EPS outlook to $30.35-$30.75.

items.title: KMI Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Natural Gas Pipeline Strength
items.summary: Kinder Morgan (KMI) beat Q3 2026 earnings expectations with adjusted EPS of 35 cents (up 20.7% YoY) and revenues of $4.53 billion (up 9.3% YoY). The company achieved record EBITDA of $2.18 billion, driven by higher natural gas transportation and gathering volumes. With a $14.4 billion project backlog and improved 2026 guidance expecting EBITDA to exceed budget by over 6%, KMI raised its quarterly dividend by 2%.

items.title: AutoZone (AZO) Up 11% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
items.summary: AutoZone reported Q4 fiscal 2026 EPS of $56.05, beating consensus estimates by 2.8%, driven by gross margin expansion. However, net sales missed expectations at $6.60 billion. The company expanded its store footprint to 8,031 locations and maintained strong commercial business momentum. Despite the earnings beat, estimates have been trending downward in the past month, and the stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with an aggregate VGM Score of D.

items.title: Costco's Last Stock Split Was in 2000. Is Its Board Close to Another?
items.summary: Costco's stock price has reached ~$994 per share since its last 2-for-1 split in January 2000, prompting investor questions about another split. However, CEO Ron Vachris and CFO Gary Millerchip have repeatedly stated there are no immediate plans, citing that fractional share purchases now make splits less economically necessary. The company continues to review the possibility with its board, but the author believes a split is unlikely in the near term and suggests a special dividend would be more beneficial to shareholders.

items.title: SpaceX Just Became an AI Company. The Numbers Prove It.
items.summary: SpaceX's AI segment (called 'super intelligence') generated $7.6 billion in Q3 revenue, up 830% year-over-year, becoming the company's largest revenue source at over 50% of sales. The segment turned profitable with $431 million in operating income after losing $1.26 billion last quarter, driven by cloud services agreements with Alphabet and Anthropic, plus the Cursor acquisition contribution of $608 million in just 6.5 weeks.

items.title: Is IBM Worth Buying as Software Growth Meets a Premium Valuation?
items.summary: IBM's software segment demonstrated solid growth with 9% revenue increase and 8% recurring revenue growth to $24.9 billion in Q3 2026. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation of 19.28X forward earnings versus its 5-year median of 17.3X. While free cash flow improved and software momentum is positive, weak consulting growth of just 2%, elevated debt of $63.8 billion, and challenges in converting AI backlog into revenue limit the investment case. IBM holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Snowflake vs. Broadcom: Which Enterprise AI Stock Is the Smarter Buy?
items.summary: Snowflake and Broadcom are both major players in the enterprise AI boom, but Snowflake emerges as the stronger pick. Snowflake benefits from accelerating product revenue growth (37% YoY), strong customer expansion, and high earnings surprises (22.77% average), earning a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). Broadcom, despite impressive AI semiconductor revenue growth (221% YoY), faces headwinds from customer concentration, margin pressure, debt burden, and execution risks, warranting a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

items.title: LVS Q3 Earnings & Revenues Miss on Soft Premium Gaming & Higher Costs
items.summary: Las Vegas Sands (LVS) reported disappointing third-quarter 2026 results with adjusted EPS of 54 cents missing estimates by 23.9% and revenues declining 3.5% year-over-year to $3.22 billion. Softer premium gaming demand in Macao and Singapore, combined with elevated operating expenses, drove property EBITDA down 16.7%. Despite the weak results, the company approved a 20% dividend increase and repurchased $950 million in shares.

items.title: GEHC Expands Theranostics Imaging With 5 Global Collaborations
items.summary: GE HealthCare announced five new global clinical collaborations to evaluate its StarGuide GX digital SPECT/CT system, a next-generation nuclear medicine imaging platform using advanced detector technology and NVIDIA computing. The system has received CE Mark approval in Europe but awaits FDA clearance in the US. The collaborations with leading institutions aim to advance quantitative imaging, dynamic imaging, and theranostics applications, supporting GEHC's competitive positioning in the growing precision oncology market.

items.title: Packaging Corp Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Favorable Price & Mix
items.summary: Packaging Corporation of America (PKG) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.04, beating consensus estimates and guidance, driven by favorable pricing in the Packaging segment and contributions from the Greif acquisition. Net sales rose 12.5% year-over-year to $2.6B with gross margin expansion to 23.2%. However, the company faces headwinds from higher labor, operating, and freight costs. Q4 guidance of $2.81 EPS reflects anticipated maintenance expenses and seasonal pressures.

items.title: Oil Prices Climb: 3 Energy Stocks Poised to Benefit From the Rally
items.summary: With crude oil prices climbing amid geopolitical tensions, three major energy companies—Chevron, Diamondback Energy, and APA Corporation—are positioned to benefit from higher oil prices. Chevron reported 20% production growth and record refinery throughput, Diamondback generated $2.3 billion in free cash flow with raised 2026 guidance, and APA exceeded oil production guidance with $738 million in free cash flow. However, benefits depend on production volumes, operating costs, and hedging strategies.

items.title: Nokia's Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI & Cloud Strength
items.summary: Nokia exceeded Q3 2026 earnings estimates by 29.45% with revenues up 10% YoY to €5.15 billion, driven by robust AI & Cloud demand surging 123%. IP Networks grew 43% and Optical Networks 18%. However, the company lowered its free cash flow conversion forecast to 35-55% from 55-75% due to working capital investments and restructuring costs. Nokia maintained its 2026 operating profit outlook of €2.1-€2.6 billion.

items.title: PHM Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates on Lower Closings & Margins
items.summary: PulteGroup (PHM) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.53 per share, missing consensus estimates and declining 14.5% year-over-year. Revenues fell 9.8% to $3.97 billion, driven by lower home closings (down 8.7%), softer average selling prices, and margin compression to 24.8%. While net new orders declined 6.5%, backlog improved 4.1% to 10,298 homes valued at $6.44 billion. The company faces persistent housing affordability challenges and rising mortgage rates.

items.title: ROAD's Florida Expansion: Can Infrastructure Demand Drive Growth?
items.summary: Construction Partners, Inc. (ROAD) acquired P&S Paving to expand its Florida footprint and strengthen its position along the I-95 corridor. The company secured $80M in Florida DOT contracts and achieved a record backlog of $3.36B with 28.2% quarterly revenue growth. However, rising energy costs, weather disruptions, and acquisition integration risks pose challenges. ROAD stock has declined 30.2% over six months and carries a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

items.title: TXN Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Analog, Data Center Demand
items.summary: Texas Instruments (TXN) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.62 per share, up 77% year-over-year and beating estimates by 9.2%. Revenues surged 28% to $6.06B, driven by strong growth in analog (32%), data center (95%), and industrial (40%+) segments. Operating margins expanded to 47.5%, and the company raised its dividend by 7% for the 23rd consecutive year. Q4 guidance ranges from $5.80B to $6.30B in revenues.

items.title: LRCX Q1 Earnings Call Highlights $200B-Plus WFE Outlook for 2027
items.summary: Lam Research (LRCX) projects wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending will exceed $200 billion in 2027, driven by AI demand and chip manufacturing complexity. The company guided December-quarter revenues to $8.6B and raised its Aether dry resist technology revenue outlook to $2.5B by decade-end. Supply chain constraints are impacting near-term shipments, though customer demand visibility extends through 2028.

items.title: Can PepsiCo's $3.5B Multipack Business Support Snack Growth?
items.summary: PepsiCo is strengthening its North American snacks business through portion-controlled formats and innovation, with volumes improving to low-single-digit growth in 2026. Keurig Dr Pepper and Coca-Cola are leveraging product innovation, affordable packaging, and portfolio diversification to drive growth amid consumer spending pressures. However, PepsiCo faces persistent margin headwinds and rising input costs, with its stock rated a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

items.title: Procter & Gamble Q1 Earnings Beat on Volume Growth & Favorable Mix
items.summary: Procter & Gamble (PG) reported Q1 FY27 core EPS of $2.00, up 1% YoY and beating consensus estimates of $1.89. Net sales rose 4% to $23.28B with 4% organic sales growth driven by volume and favorable mix. The company raised FY27 sales guidance to 2-4% but maintained core EPS guidance of $6.89-$7.11. Core operating margins contracted 80 bps due to elevated commodity costs and product reinvestments, despite 250 bps in productivity savings.

items.summary: Genuine Parts Company (GPC) continues to struggle with elevated operating expenses, geopolitical disruptions, and uneven automotive demand that are offsetting gross margin gains. The Iran conflict reduced Q3 2026 EBITDA by $16 million, while the planned 2027 separation of its Automotive and Industrial businesses is expected to add $350 million in annual corporate costs, raising execution risks.

items.title: Lam Research Q1 Earnings Beat on Systems Sales and Margin Gains
items.summary: Lam Research (LRCX) delivered exceptional Q1'27 results with EPS of $2.20 (up 74.6% YoY) and revenues of $8.22B (up 54.4% YoY), beating consensus estimates. Systems revenues surged 61.6% driven by strong NAND and foundry demand, while gross margin hit a record 52.4%. The company generated record free cash flow of $3.24B and projects Q2 EPS of $2.33, with expectations for wafer fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200B in 2027.

items.title: Investing in Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks Can be Risky, but This Might be a Great Way to Do It
items.summary: AI stocks have delivered strong returns but face rising volatility as investors question the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending. The iShares Future AI and Tech ETF (ARTY) offers diversified exposure to 50 leading AI companies across infrastructure, software, and services. While the ETF has surged 130% since its August 2024 restructure, investors should be cautious about concentration risk and its higher 0.47% expense ratio compared to passive index funds.

items.title: Own Starbucks by Nov. 13 to Qualify for Its Nov. 27 Dividend. Here's How Many Shares You'd Need for $500 in Yearly Dividends.

items.summary: Honeywell International reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.27 per share, beating consensus estimates of $2.17, but revenues of $4.99 billion missed expectations by 0.42%. items.summary: McDonald's stock has declined 20.6% in 2026, trading 29% below its 52-week high, making it one of the worst Dow performers. However, the company's 3.2% dividend yield, 50-year consecutive dividend increase streak (Dividend King status), and new NEXT strategic plan focusing on AI, store revamps, and menu simplification may present a buying opportunity for patient investors seeking inflation-hedging dividend growth.

items.title: Greg Abel Says Every Point of BNSF Profit Margin Adds About $230 Million of Cash Flow for Berkshire Hathaway
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's CEO Greg Abel is targeting significant margin improvements at BNSF railroad, stating that each 1% improvement in operating margin generates approximately $230 million in incremental operating cash flow. With current 34.5% margins and competitors operating at 38-40%, BNSF has substantial room for improvement that could potentially double its contribution to Berkshire's bottom line within five years.

items.title: Nvidia Has 80% of Its Portfolio Invested in 2 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks
items.summary: Nvidia has concentrated 80% of its investment portfolio in two AI stocks: SpaceX (33%) and Intel (47%). SpaceX shows strong AI revenue growth with $41 billion in annual customer commitments but trades at an expensive 68x sales valuation. Intel reported its fastest quarterly growth in 15 years but continues losing market share to AMD and Arm despite strong CPU demand.

items.title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Accenture, Hasbro and MSCI
items.summary: Accenture, Hasbro, and MSCI all posted strong Q3 2026 earnings results, driving positive stock reactions. Accenture reported 6% revenue growth and exceeded guidance, Hasbro saw 15% revenue growth with Magic: The Gathering sales surpassing $600 million for the first time, and MSCI delivered record results with 12-14% growth across key metrics.

items.title: Netflix Stock Is on Track for Its Worst Year Since 2022. Is It Finally a Buy?
items.summary: Netflix stock has declined 27% in 2026, approaching its worst year since 2022, despite strong business fundamentals. The company reported Q3 revenue growth of 12% to $12.9 billion and operating income up 37%, with an operating margin of 34.6%. However, revenue growth is decelerating and the company cut its 2026 ad revenue guidance from $3 billion to $2.7 billion. At a P/E ratio of 17-18, Netflix trades in line with the S&P 500 despite double-digit revenue growth and a 35% operating margin, making it worth considering for long-term investors willing to build positions gradually.

items.title: Boeing's Turnaround Just Hit a Pivot Point. Here's What It Means for the Entire Aerospace Supply Chain.
items.summary: Boeing's ramp-up of 737 MAX production to 52-57 aircraft per month is a critical pivot point for its turnaround and will significantly benefit its aerospace supply chain partners. CEO Kelly Ortberg confirmed the supply chain is in good shape, with production delays related to Boeing's own wing manufacturing rather than supplier issues. As Boeing clears pre-built inventory and reaches higher production rates in 2027, suppliers' revenue, cash flow, and profitability are expected to improve substantially.

items.title: Las Vegas Sands: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Las Vegas Sands reported Q3 2026 earnings with near-term softness in high-end customer visits across Asian markets, but management remains optimistic about long-term growth. The company has repurchased 19% of outstanding shares over 12 quarters, approved a 20% dividend increase for 2027, and gained gaming market share in Macao through strategic service investments and customer experience improvements.

items.title: Lam Research: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Lam Research reported record quarterly revenue and profitability driven by AI-induced semiconductor demand. The company raised its Aether dry resist technology revenue forecast by $1 billion to $2.5 billion by decade's end, expects its Customer Support Business Group to grow over 30% annually, and projects increased NAND wafer capacity needs due to AI storage architecture shifts toward single-level cell memory.

items.title: Zoom 以全新统一上下文层推进 AI 战略，让会议对话转化为工作成果
items.summary: Zoom Communications announced a new Unified Context Layer and multiple AI-powered products at its Zoomtopia 2026 conference. The platform aims to connect conversation history with relevant documents and data to help teams convert meetings into actionable outcomes. Zoom Virtual Agent customer numbers surged 256%, with users reporting doubled task completion speeds and 72% reporting high business impact. The company expects full-year revenue to exceed $5 billion.

items.title: ROSEN, SKILLED INVESTOR COUNSEL, Encourages AppLovin Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action – APP
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm is notifying investors in AppLovin Corporation, Beta Bionics, Inc., and Netcapital Inc. about ongoing securities class action lawsuits. AppLovin investors who purchased shares between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026 must act by November 16, 2026 deadline. The lawsuit alleges AppLovin made false statements about AI video features, overstated AI model improvements, and misrepresented the benefits of its AI platform's 'virtuous cycle' value proposition.

items.title: Cathie Wood Trimmed Ark's Alphabet Stake Even as Google Search Revenue Grew, While Ark Piled Into Rocket Lab Even After Its Neutron Launch Delay. Is Ark Betting Against the Wrong AI Winner?
items.summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Invest is reducing its Alphabet position while increasing bets on Rocket Lab despite the latter's Neutron rocket launch delay to 2027. Alphabet shows strong AI monetization through search and cloud growth, while Rocket Lab trades at a premium valuation with significant execution risks dependent on Neutron's commercial success.

items.title: ROSEN, A LEADING INVESTOR RIGHTS LAW FIRM, Encourages Bank of America Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BAC
items.summary: Rosen Law Firm has filed a securities class action lawsuit against Bank of America Corporation on behalf of investors who purchased common stock between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that Bank of America failed to disclose systemic weaknesses in its subsidiary BANA's BSA/AML compliance program, including failure to properly monitor trillions in transactions and file accurate suspicious activity reports. The firm claims defendants made materially false statements about compliance progress and expected costs, causing investor damages when the true details emerged.

items.title: Why Netflix Stock Dropped Today
items.summary: Netflix stock fell over 5% after the company cut its full-year advertising revenue forecast from $3 billion to $2.7 billion. While Q3 revenue grew 12% year-over-year to $12.9 billion and earnings per share jumped 47%, the slower growth rate and reduced ad revenue guidance disappointed investors concerned about competition from YouTube and other streaming rivals.

items.title: Brown & Brown, Inc. announces 9% increase in quarterly cash dividend rate
items.summary: Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO) announced a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.18 per share, representing a 9% increase from the previous $0.165 per share. This marks the company's 33rd consecutive annual dividend increase, payable on November 11, 2026. The insurance brokerage firm also announced it was named one of the 2026 Healthiest 100 Workplaces in America, ranking No. 25 nationally.

items.title: Q3 Earnings Beats for Meta, Tesla, IBM and T.I.
items.summary: Meta Platforms, Tesla, IBM, and Texas Instruments all beat Q3 earnings estimates. Meta reported record quarterly revenues of $64.6 billion (up 26% YoY) with EPS of $3.83, announced a 2-for-1 stock split, and raised guidance. Tesla delivered EPS of $0.48 and revenues of $28.05 billion with improved auto gross margins. IBM and Texas Instruments also exceeded consensus estimates on both earnings and revenues.

items.title: Stock Market Today, Oct. 21: AT&T Beats Earnings on Strong Fiber Growth, Raises 2026 Profit Outlook
items.summary: AT&T reported better-than-expected earnings with record internet additions and raised its 2026 profit outlook, but the stock fell 6.45% as investors focused on higher spending needs and growing competition from SpaceX's direct-to-device connectivity plans. The company also agreed to sell its Mexico wireless unit for $2 billion.

items.title: Netflix Is Down 38% Since Completing Its 10-For-1 Stock Split. Here's Why the Sell-Off Is Worsening After Its Latest Earnings.
items.summary: Netflix stock has fallen 37.9% since completing its 10-for-1 stock split in November 2025, with further declines following Q3 2026 earnings. While the company reported solid revenue growth of 11.8% and improved operating margins, it lowered full-year ad revenue guidance by 10% due to slower ad product rollout. The sell-off reflects concerns about slowing growth, increased competition from mobile-focused platforms like YouTube and TikTok, and the impact of recent price increases on price-sensitive subscribers. However, Netflix maintains a strong balance sheet with $8.19 billion in cash and trades at a relatively attractive 17x forward earnings multiple.

items.summary: Honeywell Aerospace investors have until November 23, 2026 to seek lead plaintiff status in a securities fraud class action. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased shares between June 29 and September 1, 2026. The company allegedly failed to disclose material adverse facts including supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, cybersecurity compliance issues with defense contracts, and a $2 million false Claims Act settlement. The stock fell 23.16% on August 6, 2026 following disappointing earnings and guidance cuts.

items.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific raised its full-year 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 4% following strong Q3 results with $12.14 billion in revenue and 6% organic growth. The company is leveraging AI integration to reduce manual laboratory setup time by 90%, accelerating workflows and boosting recurring sales. Strategic acquisitions like Clario are expanding clinical development capabilities and creating revenue synergies, positioning the company for durable margin expansion amid strengthening biopharmaceutical research activity.

items.title: Unveiling Cincinnati Financial (CINF) Q3 Outlook: Wall Street Estimates for Key Metrics
items.summary: Cincinnati Financial is expected to report Q3 earnings of $1.99 per share, down 30.2% year-over-year, with revenues forecast at $3.03 billion, up 5.5%. Key metrics show mixed results: investment income rising 9.6%, earned premiums up 5%, but the combined ratio deteriorating to 96.4% from 88.2%, indicating higher losses and expenses across insurance segments.

items.title: Skydance Trades at a Fraction of Netflix's Valuation. Is the Discount Deserved?
items.summary: After acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery, Skydance trades at roughly one-eighth Netflix's valuation. However, the discount appears justified given Skydance's $78.9 billion net debt (more than double its market cap), single-digit operating margins, and shrinking cable networks, compared to Netflix's clean balance sheet, powerful cash generation, and 33.4% operating margins.

items.summary: As October 2026 earnings season approaches, five companies with Zacks Rank #1 and Growth Score A ratings stand out for combining strong revenue growth with high operating margins. (NASDAQ: XTIA) alleging that company executives made materially false statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts during the Class Period (April 15, 2026 - August 17, 2026). The complaint claims senior executives engaged in undisclosed activities that required Board review, raising doubts about disclosure controls and the company's ability to file timely earnings reports. Investors who purchased XTI Aerospace securities during this period are encouraged to join the lawsuit, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 27, 2026.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Honeywell Aerospace, Inc. alleging that the company made materially false statements and failed to disclose material adverse facts during the Class Period (June 29 - September 1, 2026). The complaint alleges undisclosed supplier concentration risks, supply constraints, a false Claims Act investigation related to cybersecurity compliance on government contracts, and that positive statements about the company lacked reasonable basis. Investors who purchased Honeywell securities during this period are urged to join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of November 23, 2026.

items.title: Is Berkshire Hathaway's Greg Abel Is Changing the Script? Here's the Latest Tech Stock He Just Bought.
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway, under CEO Greg Abel, has expanded its investment in Bending Spoons with an additional $330 million purchase, bringing its stake to 4%. Bending Spoons is an Italian holding company that acquires and improves underperforming tech companies like Vimeo, Evernote, and AOL. While the company shows strong growth (126% revenue increase in Q2), it carries significant debt ($4.09 billion net debt). Abel's move signals a willingness to venture into tech and international opportunities beyond Berkshire's traditional industries.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against AST SpaceMobile, Inc. alleging securities fraud. The complaint claims the company made false statements regarding its capital requirements, liquidity position, competitive standing in the satellite direct-to-cell market, and user adoption rates between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026. Investors have until November 13, 2026 to request lead plaintiff status.

items.title: No, I'm Not Selling You My Netflix Stock Today
items.summary: Netflix stock fell to a two-year low after Q3 earnings beat expectations but guidance disappointed. Revenue grew 11.8% to $12.87B and earnings rose 44% to $0.87/share, but Q4 guidance projects only 11.5% revenue growth and 15% earnings growth—the weakest performance in over three years. Despite six consecutive quarters of decelerating growth and key executive departures, the author maintains his long-term position, citing Netflix's historical resilience and current valuation at 17x forward earnings.

items.title: AppLovin vs. Pinterest: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares AppLovin and Pinterest as investment opportunities in the digital advertising space. AppLovin demonstrates explosive growth with 70% revenue increase, exceptional profitability (60.8% net margin), and strong free cash flow, making it the author's preferred choice. Pinterest offers a massive 640 million user base and improving AI-powered ad tools but faces challenges with lower profitability (9.9% net margin) and GAAP net losses, though it maintains a conservative balance sheet.

items.title: Wabtec Q3 Earnings Beat on Margin Expansion, Revenues Miss
items.summary: Wabtec Corporation reported Q3 2026 earnings of $2.83 per share, beating consensus estimates by 4%, with revenues of $3.12 billion slightly missing expectations. The company raised its full-year 2026 earnings guidance to $10.85-$11.05 per share. Both Freight and Transit segments showed strong margin expansion (190 and 260 basis points respectively), driven by organic growth, acquisitions, and operational efficiencies. Total backlog reached $31.44 billion, up 22.9% year-over-year.

items.title: PAHC or SYK: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two medical products sector stocks reveals Phibro Animal Health (PAHC) as the superior value opportunity. PAHC holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) with a forward P/E of 11.12 and Value grade of B, while Stryker (SYK) has a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) with a forward P/E of 20.39 and Value grade of D. PAHC's stronger earnings outlook and more attractive valuation metrics make it the better choice for value investors.

items.title: KUBTY or DE: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two manufacturing farm equipment companies reveals that Kubota Corp. (KUBTY) presents a better value opportunity than Deere (DE) based on valuation metrics and earnings outlook. KUBTY has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with a forward P/E of 10.74 and Value grade of A, while DE has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a forward P/E of 34.91 and Value grade of D.

items.title: CBZ vs. EFX: Which Stock Should Value Investors Buy Now?
items.summary: A comparison of two consulting services stocks reveals that CBIZ (CBZ) presents a better value opportunity than Equifax (EFX). CBZ has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) with improving earnings outlook, a lower forward P/E of 13.17 versus EFX's 20.79, and a superior Value grade of A compared to EFX's C grade.

items.title: ZTS vs. ICCC: Which Animal Health Stock Is the Better Investment Bet?
items.summary: Zoetis (ZTS) and ImmuCell (ICCC) operate in animal health but with different profiles. Zoetis offers diversification across companion animals, livestock, and diagnostics but faces near-term headwinds from declining companion animal demand and reduced 2026 guidance. ImmuCell shows stronger recent growth with 20.9% sales increases and expanding market share in calf scours prevention, but carries higher execution risks due to narrow product focus and margin pressures during manufacturing expansion.

items.title: ISRG Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Pricing and Growth Strategy
items.summary: Intuitive Surgical reported Q3 2026 earnings beating consensus estimates with $3.05B in revenue. The company announced planned instrument pricing reductions of 3-5% to expand robotic surgery adoption, narrowed 2026 procedure growth guidance to 14-15%, and raised gross margin outlook to 68.7-69.3%. U.S. procedure growth slowed to 10% while international placements surged 29%, with strong expansion in Europe and Asia.

items.title: ELV Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates on Carelon Strength, Raises 2026 Outlook
items.summary: Elevance Health reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $6.99, significantly beating estimates by 50%, with revenue reaching $50.4B. The Carelon segment drove growth with 5.4% revenue increase and 17.2% operating gain growth. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $29.00 and increased its earnings baseline to at least $26.75.

items.title: These 3 Stocks Surged Following Strong Quarterly Results
items.summary: Three major companies delivered positive Q3 earnings results. Accenture reported 6% YoY revenue growth to $18.7B with strong bookings of $22.2B. Hasbro posted 15% YoY revenue growth to $1.6B, with Magic: The Gathering sales exceeding $600M for the first time, prompting raised FY26 guidance. MSCI achieved record results with 12% YoY revenue growth to $892M and record asset-based fees, with all three stocks experiencing favorable post-earnings reactions.

items.title: Pre-Markets in Green on Strong Earnings Results
items.summary: Markets open higher ahead of major Mag 7 earnings reports. SpaceX posts impressive Q3 results with 161% revenue growth. Early morning earnings from NextEra Energy, Abbott Labs, and CME Group show mixed results, with Abbott declining on nutrition spinoff concerns. Meta and Tesla earnings expected after close, with Meta facing -52.4% earnings decline despite strong revenue growth, while Tesla carries a Sell rating heading into its report.

items.title: PM Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Pricing & Sales Growth
items.summary: Philip Morris International (PM) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.36 (up 5.4% YoY) and revenues of $11.44 billion (up 5.5% YoY), both beating consensus estimates. Strong combustible pricing and smoke-free product demand, particularly ZYN in the U.S., drove growth. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.29-$8.44 and maintained its 5-7% organic revenue growth forecast, while also increasing its quarterly dividend by 8.8%.

items.title: DHR Q3 Earnings Beat on Biotechnology Strength, Sales in Line
items.summary: Danaher Corporation reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.11, beating estimates by 9.9%, with revenues of $6.55 billion in line with expectations. The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.57-$8.62 and expects 2.5% core revenue growth. Diagnostics segment sales jumped 17% driven by acquisitions, though respiratory testing revenues declined significantly from $500M to $350M year-over-year.

items.title: Is Raymond James Well-Positioned to Sustain Strong Capital Returns?
items.summary: Raymond James Financial (RJF) returned nearly $2 billion to shareholders over the trailing 12 months through dividends and share buybacks, while maintaining strong capital positions to support organic growth and strategic acquisitions. The company announced an 8% dividend increase and repurchased 9.8 million shares, supported by solid earnings growth projections of 13.8% for fiscal 2026 and 17.1% for fiscal 2027. However, regulatory capital requirements and elevated expenses remain risk factors.

items.title: NextEra Energy Q3 Earnings Beat on FPL Strength, Revenues Miss
items.summary: NextEra Energy (NEE) reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.24, beating consensus estimates by 3.3%, driven by strong performance from Florida Power & Light and NextEra Energy Resources. The company added 3.7 GW to its renewables backlog and maintained its 2026 EPS guidance of $3.92-$4.02. However, total revenues missed expectations. NEE continues advancing its pending merger with Dominion Energy, expected to close in H2 2027.

items.title: Steel Dynamics: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Steel Dynamics reported record Q3 2026 quarterly steel shipments of 3.8 million tons with mills operating at 92% capacity, significantly outperforming the domestic industry average of 80%. The company resolved aluminum production bottlenecks and is benefiting from strong demand in nonresidential construction and domestic manufacturing reshoring, with fabrication order backlogs up 50% year-over-year. Management expects higher-margin cash generation as new capacity ramps up.

items.title: MMM Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Deals and Higher Outlook
items.summary: 3M raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $9.10-$9.15, driven by strong industrial demand, expanding data center opportunities, and productivity improvements. The company expanded its Amazon partnership targeting $6 billion in cumulative sales over 7 years and achieved 110 basis points of operating margin expansion to 26.2%. However, consumer electronics weakness persists, particularly in LCD displays and Chinese device manufacturers.

items.title: CAT Keeps Dividend Unchanged: Is Another Hike on the Horizon?
items.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) maintained its $1.63 quarterly dividend and returned $7.9 billion to shareholders in H1 2026. The company raised its full-year 2026 sales growth outlook to mid-to-high teens, supported by a record $72 billion backlog and improved business conditions. CAT has increased its dividend for 33 consecutive years and maintains a sustainable dividend profile with a 0.30 dividend-to-free-cash-flow ratio.

items.title: Is it Wise to Retain Public Storage Stock in Your Portfolio Now?
items.summary: Public Storage (PSA) is expanding through strategic acquisitions, including a $1.2 billion Canadian portfolio purchase, and leveraging AI-powered tools to drive growth. However, the company faces challenges from declining same-store revenues (-0.6% YoY), rising interest expenses ($84.8M in Q2), and competitive pressure from peers like Extra Space Storage and CubeSmart. Management expects same-store revenue recovery by Q4, though the pace remains uncertain.

items.title: GE Vernova (GEV) Earnings Expected to Grow: Should You Buy?
items.summary: GE Vernova (GEV) is expected to report Q3 2026 earnings of $4.03 per share with revenues of $12.1 billion on October 28. The company shows a positive Earnings ESP of +5.47% combined with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting a likely earnings beat. However, the company missed estimates significantly in the last quarter with a -22.08% surprise.

items.title: NUE Rides on Expansion Actions, Higher Steel Prices & Acquisitions
items.summary: Nucor Corporation is expanding production capacity with major projects including a 3 million ton per annum sheet mill in West Virginia expected to complete in late 2026. The company projects Q3 2026 earnings of $5.55-$5.65 per share, driven by higher steel prices and volumes. U.S. steel prices have surged above $1,300 per short ton recently, benefiting major producers. Peer steel companies Steel Dynamics, Cleveland-Cliffs, and ArcelorMittal are also reporting strong earnings guidance and improved market conditions.

items.title: NOC's Q3 Earnings Call Highlights 2027 Growth and B-21 Spending
items.summary: Northrop Grumman raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $29.35-$29.75 and projects 5%-7% sales growth in 2027 with expanding margins. The company reported Q3 EPS of $7.89, exceeding expectations, and maintains a record $109.6 billion backlog. Management is investing $2.1 billion in B-21 production capacity while preserving $3.3-$3.7 billion free cash flow outlook, though acknowledges execution risks and timing uncertainties.

items.title: General Motors Q3 Earnings Call Weighs 2027 Cost Risks Against Cash Gains
items.summary: General Motors raised its 2026 automotive free cash flow guidance to $11.5B-$12.5B following Q3 earnings and revenue beats. However, the company warned that sustained commodity inflation could add $1B-$1.5B in EBIT pressure for 2027, potentially complicating earnings growth. GM expects a 35,000-pickup Q4 shortfall due to changeovers and plans flat pickup production in 2027 before growth resumes in 2028. The company is betting on next-generation Silverado and Sierra pickups, expanding software/services revenue, and achieving EV cost reductions to drive future growth.

items.summary: NextEra Energy (NEE) reported quarterly earnings of $1.24 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $1.20 and surpassing the prior year's $1.13. The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 by 14.5% year-to-date and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating, suggesting near-term performance in line with the market.

items.title: Capital One Stock Gains as Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Higher NII
items.summary: Capital One reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $6.69 per share, beating consensus estimates of $5.45, with a 12% year-over-year increase. Net interest income rose 4% to $12.89 billion and net interest margin expanded 5 basis points to 8.41%. However, the company faced headwinds from higher expenses (up 7%), increased provisions (up 7%), and sequential deposit declines. Credit quality improved with net charge-offs falling 10% year-over-year. Capital One carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: If I Could Only Invest $500 in AI This Month, I'd Buy This 1 Stock.
items.summary: Netlist has secured major patent settlement deals with Samsung and Micron worth $897 million and $600 million respectively over five years, generating nearly $100 million in annual recurring revenue. The company is leveraging these proceeds to scale its AI memory hardware business, with products like CXL NVvault addressing memory bottlenecks in AI systems. With a market cap of $2.1 billion and strong growth momentum, Netlist is positioned similarly to Rambus and could see significant upside from hyperscaler deals and agentic AI adoption.

items.title: Netflix Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Ad Revenue View Trimmed
items.summary: Netflix reported Q3 2026 EPS of 87 cents, up 49% YoY and beating consensus by 6.1%, with operating margin expanding to 34.6%. However, the company trimmed its 2026 ad revenue outlook to $2.7B and free cash flow forecast to $12B due to slower-than-expected ad product rollout. Subscription revenue growth and strong performance in India offset advertising headwinds.

items.title: Capital One: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
items.summary: Capital One reported $1.8 billion in annualized Discover integration synergies, exceeding initial timelines. The company is accelerating debit account conversions and cost reductions while increasing marketing spend to drive customer acquisition across credit cards and national banking. Management is investing heavily in AI and technology to strengthen premium customer relationships and maintain credit discipline.

Microsoft's cloud business grows more slowly at 43% but maintains strong free cash flow of $20 billion and lower debt levels. While Oracle has greater upside potential if execution succeeds, Microsoft's financial flexibility makes it the better 5-year investment choice due to its ability to weather potential delays in AI infrastructure projects.

items.title: If Alphabet Does This on Oct. 28, the Stock Could Skyrocket
items.summary: Alphabet is expected to report strong Q3 earnings on Oct. 28, with Google Cloud as the key catalyst. Google Cloud's revenue growth accelerated to 82% in Q2, significantly outpacing competitors Microsoft Azure (43%) and Amazon Web Services (37%). The growth is driven by massive AI workload demand and Alphabet's $195-205 billion capital expenditure investment in data centers. Custom TPUs and upcoming revenue from selling these units could further boost cloud growth. At 27x operating income, Alphabet appears fairly valued, with stock upside dependent on earnings delivery.

items.title: Comcast Trades at 6 Times Earnings and Yields 6%. Does It Deserve to Be One of the Cheapest S&P 500 Dividend Stocks, or Is This a No-Brainer Buying Opportunity?
items.summary: Comcast trades at a low valuation of 6x forward earnings with a 6% dividend yield, but the article advises caution. items.summary: Marvell Technology's 17% stock decline during a chip-sector sell-off presents a buying opportunity, according to the article. Despite risks including lumpy revenue and customer concentration, Nvidia's $2 billion investment in Marvell preferred stock validates the company's strategic importance in AI infrastructure.

items.title: Bloom Energy vs. Oracle: Which AI Infrastructure Stock Is the Better Buy After the Jupiter Setback?
items.summary: Oracle and Bloom Energy are both involved in Project Jupiter, a massive AI data center in New Mexico facing delays and local opposition. Oracle cited 'force majeure' to protect itself if the project fails, putting it at greater risk than Bloom Energy. While Oracle's entire data center project is at stake, Bloom Energy's fuel cells represent a smaller component that could be easily redirected to other customers. Bloom Energy is positioned as the better investment choice for those concerned about Project Jupiter's completion.

items.title: Nike vs. Procter & Gamble: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Nike and Procter & Gamble as investment options in 2026. The author recommends Procter & Gamble as the more stable choice for long-term investors, citing its recession-resistant business model and 70-year dividend increase streak, while suggesting investors wait for Nike to show sustained earnings improvements before investing.

items.summary: JPMorgan and Citigroup reported Q3 earnings with contrasting profiles. JPMorgan demonstrated earnings resilience with 6% net income growth, benefiting from higher net interest income and loan growth, while maintaining industry-leading profitability and a strong balance sheet. Citigroup delivered robust 40% net income growth as its multiyear restructuring gains momentum, with improved efficiency ratios and cost discipline. JPMorgan trades at a premium valuation (13.41X forward P/E) reflecting its stability, while Citigroup's discounted valuation (9.74X) presents greater upside potential if its turnaround succeeds. Both stocks carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

items.title: Expand Energy Stock Declines 17% YTD: How Should Investors Play It?
items.summary: Expand Energy (EXE), the largest U.S. independent natural gas producer formed from the Chesapeake-Southwestern merger, has underperformed its sector by 17.4% YTD despite projected 40.8% earnings growth in 2026. While the company benefits from a discounted valuation, the $1.25B Twin Eagle acquisition, and strong balance sheet improvements, significant headwinds including natural gas price volatility, high capital expenditures ($2.75-2.95B), rising transportation costs, and integration risks warrant a cautious Hold rating.

items.title: Better Artificial Intelligence Stock for 2026: Astera Labs vs. Marvell Technology
items.summary: The article compares two semiconductor companies powering AI data centers: Astera Labs, a high-speed connectivity specialist with 115% revenue growth but high customer concentration (70% from one customer), and Marvell Technology, a broader semiconductor provider with 42% growth, lower valuation multiples, and confidence in reaching $70-90 billion in revenue by 2031. items.title: SEC Approves HOOD-Linked KPI Contracts: A New Growth Avenue Unlocked?
items.summary: The SEC approved Cboe Global Markets' proposal to list binary options tied to company-specific KPIs, with Robinhood Markets expected to become the first retail brokerage offering these contracts covering over 100 metrics across 23 companies. While this presents a new revenue opportunity aligned with Robinhood's active-trading strategy, near-term monetization is limited by pending clearing approvals and fee waivers through 2026. Regulatory uncertainty around event-driven products and the need for sustained customer adoption also present challenges.

items.title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Innventure, Inc. Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
items.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Innventure, Inc. and certain officers for alleged securities law violations. Investors who purchased securities between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026 can join the case, with a lead plaintiff deadline of October 27, 2026.

items.title: VEOEY or WM: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
items.summary: In a comparison of two waste removal services stocks, Veolia Environnement SA (VEOEY) emerges as the better value option compared to Waste Management (WM). items.title: Figma vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares Figma and Palantir Technologies as investment options in 2026. items.title: CRDO vs. COHR: Which AI Connectivity Stock Is the Better Buy?
items.summary: Credo Technology (CRDO) and Coherent Corp (COHR) are both capitalizing on AI data center expansion through different approaches. items.title: Morgan Stanley Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Wealth and AI Strategy
items.summary: Morgan Stanley reported Q3 2026 EPS of $3.03 on $20.34B in revenues, beating estimates. The firm achieved record Wealth Management revenues of $9.1B with $232B in net new assets. items.title: BNY Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Fee Income & NII Growth
items.summary: Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.37, beating consensus estimates of $2.26, with a 24.1% year-over-year increase. Total revenues rose 11.7% to $5.68B, driven by higher fee revenues and net interest income. However, the company faces headwinds from rising expenses, deposit margin compression, and net outflows in assets under management. Capital ratios declined compared to the prior year.

items.title: MMM Q3 Earnings on Deck: How to Approach the Stock Now?
items.summary: 3M is expected to report Q3 2026 revenue of $6.60 billion and EPS of $2.41 on October 20. However, weakness in the Consumer segment and elevated R&D costs pose challenges. The stock trades at a premium valuation compared to industry peers.

items.title: Archer Daniels' Sweetener Weakness: Can Ethanol Offset It?
items.summary: Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) reported a 22% year-over-year increase in Carbohydrate Solutions operating profit to $411 million in Q2 2026, driven by strong ethanol margins and policy incentives that offset weakness in liquid sweeteners. ADM raised its expected 2026 benefit from the 45Z policy to $250 million from $150 million, supporting its outlook despite ongoing challenges in North American sweetener volumes.

items.summary: As AI adoption shifts from infrastructure building to productivity gains, Synopsys emerges as a potential winner by providing chip design software and IP. items.title: HPQ Jumps 37% YTD: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: HP Inc. (HPQ) has gained 36.7% year-to-date and trades at a significant valuation discount with a forward P/S ratio of 0.46 versus industry average of 8.58. HPQ received a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating based on product innovation, premiumization strategy, and attractive valuation metrics.

items.title: Can Gaming Pipeline and Activision Add Momentum to Microsoft Stock?
items.summary: Microsoft is betting on major fall gaming releases, including Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, to revive its struggling Xbox business. items.title: Block's AI-Powered Kiosk Launch to Drive Revenue and Merchant Growth
items.summary: Block, Inc. has introduced Square Kiosk, an AI-powered self-service ordering system designed for quick-service restaurants. The kiosk features a 21.5-inch touchscreen, conversational AI voice capabilities, integrated payments, and personalized loyalty features. Priced at $1,999 with a $99 monthly software fee, the product aims to streamline ordering, improve customer experiences, and increase transaction values through intelligent add-on suggestions. The launch is expected to strengthen Block's position in restaurant technology and support revenue growth through hardware sales, recurring software fees, and increased payment processing volumes.

items.title: Wells Fargo Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Higher Interest Income Outlook
items.summary: Wells Fargo reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.87 per share, beating consensus estimates, and reaffirmed full-year net interest income guidance of $50 billion. items.title: S&P 500 ETFs Defy Rate Worries as Earnings Outlook Strengthens

items.summary: Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Meta are projected to spend $745 billion on capital expenditures this year, primarily for data center infrastructure. items.summary: Carnival Corporation posted record Q3 2026 results with $8.4 billion in revenue and $1.9 billion in net income, with strong demand for cruise travel continuing despite economic concerns. The stock trades at a forward P/E ratio of 8.4, representing a 50% discount to the S&P 500, suggesting potential upside if current positive trends persist. items.summary: Bank of America raised its quarterly dividend by 14% to $0.32 per share ($1.28 annually), offering a 2.4% yield. items.summary: CoreWeave is a rapidly growing AI-focused cloud provider expanding at 112% year-over-year, compared to AWS's 37% growth. However, AWS maintains a massive 20x size advantage with $42.2B in quarterly revenue versus CoreWeave's $2.1B. At current growth rates, it would take CoreWeave nearly seven years to match AWS's revenue. While CoreWeave presents significant upside potential if it achieves profitability comparable to AWS's 39% operating margin, it currently lacks profitability and faces execution risks.

The firm is seeking a lead plaintiff by the October 27, 2026 deadline.

items.title: Is SoundHound AI a Buy After the LivePerson Deal?
items.summary: SoundHound AI has significantly expanded its enterprise opportunity through the acquisition of LivePerson. The key question for investors is whether the company can successfully convert this larger customer base into cross-selling opportunities, higher recurring revenue, and improved financial performance before mounting losses, declining legacy revenue, and shareholder dilution undermine the investment thesis.

items.title: Why ExxonMobil's Venezuela Warning Could Matter for Energy Investors Right Now
items.summary: ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods initially called Venezuela 'uninvestable,' but the company is now reportedly in talks to invest in Venezuelan oilfields. However, Venezuela's production capacity remains severely constrained at 1.2 million barrels per day versus its historical peak of 3.5 million, meaning any investment there won't materially impact global oil prices in the near term. For ExxonMobil investors, Venezuela represents a potential bonus rather than a core growth driver, with the company's primary growth engines being its operations in Guyana and the Permian Basin.

items.title: NASDAQ: DUOL: Kessler Topaz Meltzer & Check, LLP Announces the Filing of a Securities Fraud Class Action Lawsuit Against Duolingo, Inc.
items.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit has been filed against Duolingo, Inc. for investors who purchased stock between May 2, 2025 and February 26, 2026. The lawsuit alleges material misstatements regarding monetization strategies and user friction that negatively impacted daily active user (DAU) growth. Duolingo's stock declined significantly following disappointing Q3 results (DAU growth fell to 36% from 49%), a CFO resignation, and weak Q4 guidance showing only 20% DAU growth for 2026.

items.title: Warren Buffett Held Wells Fargo Stock for More Than 30 Years Before Selling It. Here's the Lesson for Bank Stocks.
items.summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway held Wells Fargo stock for nearly 30 years starting in 1989, but exited the position in 2022 following the bank's 2016 phony accounts scandal. While CEO Charlie Scharf successfully turned the bank around with operational improvements and regulatory compliance, Buffett had already sold due to frustration with the board and uncertainty about the turnaround timeline. The case illustrates the importance of reputation in banking and the challenge of identifying viable long-term turnaround opportunities.

items.title: Sundar Pichai Reported Alphabet's Cloud Revenue Grew 82% to $24.8 Billion Last Quarter, With the Gemini App Reaching 950 Million Monthly Users. Is Google Cloud Becoming a Bigger Growth Driver Than Search?
items.summary: Alphabet's Google Cloud revenue surged 82% to $24.8 billion in Q2, significantly outpacing search revenue growth of 17%. With 950 million Gemini app users and a $514 billion revenue backlog, Google Cloud is emerging as a primary growth driver for Alphabet's AI-focused future, though search still accounts for over half of total revenue.

items.title: Netflix Is Reportedly Cutting 5% of Its Staff. Its 2022 Layoffs Came Days After the Stock Bottomed.
items.summary: Netflix is reportedly planning to cut around 5% of its ~16,000-person workforce (approximately 800 jobs) as early as next week. The layoffs aim to align non-content spending growth with slowing revenue growth. Unlike the 2022 layoffs that coincided with a stock bottom, the current situation differs: Netflix maintains double-digit revenue growth and a 33.4% operating margin, suggesting this is a margin optimization move rather than a defensive measure. The stock trades at 19x forward earnings, with revenue growth cooling from 18% to 13% year-over-year.

items.title: Why C3.ai, Inc. (AI) Outpaced the Stock Market Today
items.summary: C3.ai, Inc. (AI) closed at $11.53, up 1.68% in the latest session, outperforming the S&P 500's 0.6% gain. The stock has gained 8.31% over the past month. items.summary: Edelson Lechtzin LLP is investigating a class action lawsuit against Southern Company following a data breach affecting approximately 400,000 customer accounts across Georgia Power, Alabama Power, and Mississippi Power. The law firm is offering free case evaluations to affected customers.

items.title: Buy, Sell, or Hold Delta Air Lines Stock After Q3 Earnings?
items.summary: Delta Air Lines reported disappointing Q3 results, missing earnings and revenue expectations despite record revenue and strong travel demand. Surging fuel costs (up 62% YoY to $4.14B) pressured profitability, prompting management to slash full-year EPS guidance from $6.50-$7.50 to $5.10-$5.60. The airline expects to absorb approximately $6 billion in additional fuel costs this year, highlighting industry-wide challenges.

items.title: DAL Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Higher Fuel Costs Hurt Margins
items.summary: Delta Air Lines reported Q3 2026 earnings of $1.72 per share, missing estimates by 4.44% as fuel costs surged 62%. While adjusted revenues climbed 16% to $17.59 billion driven by strong passenger demand and premium sales, the company cut its full-year 2026 EPS outlook to $5.10-$5.60 from $6.50-$7.50 due to elevated fuel prices and rising non-fuel expenses.

items.title: Cerebras Systems vs. IonQ: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: The article compares two specialized hardware companies: Cerebras Systems, which builds AI-accelerating wafer-scale processors and recently achieved profitability with $510M revenue but faces competitive pressure from Nvidia; and IonQ, a quantum computing leader with 202% revenue growth to $130M but still unprofitable with $510M net losses. The author recommends IonQ for 2026 due to its diversified customer base, expanding backlog, and fewer near-term competitive concerns, despite both being speculative early-stage investments.

items.title: Prediction: A $5,000 Investment Split Between Nvidia and Broadcom Will Triple by 2028
items.summary: Nvidia and Broadcom are positioned for significant growth through 2028, with both companies forecasting substantial revenue increases driven by AI infrastructure demand. Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenue to reach $230 billion by 2028, while Nvidia projects 70% annual revenue growth. Based on these growth trajectories and historical valuations, an equal investment in both stocks could potentially triple by 2028.

items.title: Nvidia and AMD Lead the AI Market. 1 Chip Stock Has Far Greater Upside.
items.summary: While AMD has outperformed Nvidia in 2026 with a 200% rise versus Nvidia's 30%, the article argues Nvidia offers greater future upside. AMD's valuation has become stretched with its forward P/E ratio surging, and despite strong data center growth of 107%, it lags Nvidia's 117% growth. Nvidia's upcoming Vera Rubin chip architecture and projected 70% revenue growth in 2027 position it as the better investment despite being the world's largest company.

items.title: J.B. Hunt Gears Up for Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services is set to report Q3 2026 earnings on October 15, facing headwinds from rising freight costs, wage inflation, and weakness in its Final Mile Services segment. With an Earnings ESP of -6.99% and a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell), the company is unlikely to beat consensus estimates. The Truckload and Integrated Capacity Solutions businesses also face margin pressures amid challenging market conditions.

items.title: Can Monaco's Expanding Footprint Drive Molson Coors' Revenues?
items.summary: Molson Coors (TAP) acquired Monaco Cocktails through Atomic Brands to expand in the ready-to-drink spirits category. Monaco's first full quarter showed sales and profits ahead of expectations, with presence in five states offering significant expansion potential. Both Monaco and Fever-Tree are on track to contribute 1-2% of TAP's net sales. TAP stock trades at a discount valuation (7.68X forward P/E vs. industry average 14.18X) but has underperformed its sector over six months.

items.title: GE Aerospace Down 15% in 3 Months: Is This a Buying Opportunity?
items.summary: GE Aerospace shares have declined 15% in three months, but strong commercial engine demand, robust Q2 2026 revenue growth of 27%, and raised free cash flow guidance to $8.9-$9.2 billion support a positive outlook. However, elevated valuation at 34.79X forward P/E (above industry average of 27.16X), rising debt levels of $19.2 billion, and surging costs present risks. The stock maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating despite trading below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages.

items.title: PepsiCo Just Reported Earnings. Here's What Investors Need to Know.
items.summary: PepsiCo beat Q3 earnings expectations with 3.1% organic revenue growth and a 3.7% stock price increase, despite cutting full-year EPS guidance to 2.5%-3.5%. The company faces challenges in North America beverages and snacks due to GLP-1 drug impacts and consumer pushback, but international segments remain strong. With a 4.6% dividend yield and P/E of 15, the stock may appeal to defensive dividend investors seeking recovery potential.

items.title: SPCX to Acquire 800 MHz Spectrum for Superior Network: Buy the Stock?
items.summary: SpaceX has agreed to acquire Grain Management's 800 MHz spectrum portfolio to enhance Starlink Mobile's connectivity capabilities. The low-band spectrum will enable a hybrid satellite-terrestrial network, improving indoor coverage and reliability. Combined with previously acquired 2 GHz spectrum from EchoStar, this positions SpaceX to compete as a major U.S. wireless operator while expanding its AI infrastructure ambitions.

items.title: 3 Top-Ranked Stocks Breaking Records on AI-Related Demand
items.summary: Micron, NVIDIA, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise have all posted stellar quarterly earnings driven by robust AI-related demand. Micron reported record Q4 revenue of $54.2 billion with strong pricing tailwinds, NVIDIA saw data center revenue surge 117% year-over-year to $89 billion, and HPE achieved record quarterly revenue of $12.2 billion with accelerating growth. All three companies maintain Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) ratings with bullish earnings estimate revisions and positive near-term outlooks.

items.title: Starbucks Explores CMG Deal: Smart Move or Costly Gamble?
items.summary: Starbucks has reportedly consulted advisers about acquiring Chipotle Mexican Grill, according to a Financial Times report. While the deal could diversify Starbucks' business and leverage CEO Brian Niccol's prior experience at Chipotle, concerns exist about financing requirements, integration challenges, and potential distraction from the company's ongoing turnaround strategy. No deal has been confirmed.

items.title: Reasons to Hold Veeva Systems Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: Veeva Systems (VEEV) delivered strong Q2 fiscal 2027 results, beating estimates and raising its full-year outlook, driven by expanding Vault CRM adoption with 12 of top 20 biopharmas committed and over 180 customers live. The company is advancing AI initiatives with Veeva Falcon attracting early adopters. However, market saturation in the life sciences CRM space and intensifying competition from traditional and AI-powered platforms could constrain future growth rates.

items.title: Viatris to Buy Pacira for $1.65B to Expand Non-Opioid Pain Portfolio
items.summary: Viatris (VTRS) has agreed to acquire Pacira BioSciences (PCRX) for $1.65 billion in cash at $36.50 per share, expected to close by end of 2026. The acquisition adds two marketed pain therapies (Exparel and Zilretta) generating $350.5 million in H1 2026 sales, plus a mid-stage gene therapy candidate (PCRX-201) for knee osteoarthritis. The deal is expected to be immediately accretive to Viatris' financial metrics and strengthen its non-opioid pain management portfolio.

items.title: EMCOR Stock Trades at a Premium: Should Investors Buy or Steer Clear?
items.summary: EMCOR Group (EME) reported strong first-half 2026 results with 19.7% revenue growth to $9.78 billion, driven by robust demand for data centers, AI infrastructure, and healthcare projects. The company raised full-year guidance and achieved record backlog of $17.14 billion. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation (21.46x forward P/E) compared to peers, and faces headwinds from inflation, labor shortages, and supply-chain disruptions.

items.title: BlackBerry Jumps 13.3% in a Week as QNX and Earnings Momentum Build
items.summary: BlackBerry (BB) surged 13.3% in a week following stronger-than-expected earnings, with QNX revenues jumping 27.3% to a record $80.3 million and adjusted EBITDA rising 41.5%. The company raised fiscal 2027 guidance across revenue, EBITDA, and operating cash flow. However, the stock trades at 8.0X EV/Sales versus its 5-year median of 3.8X, creating a higher execution bar. Secure Communications showed weakness with declining net retention at 91%, and the company faces contract-timing risks. BB holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with strong Growth and Momentum scores but weak Value score.

items.title: PEP Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Margin Pressure and Growth Plans
items.summary: PepsiCo reduced its 2026 core EPS growth guidance to 2.5%-3.5% from 5%-7% due to rising input costs, weaker margins, and unfavorable product mix. While the company reported strong international growth (8% organic revenue increase) and showed signs of North American snack recovery, beverage segment weakness and expiring commodity hedges remain concerns. Management plans increased brand investments and distribution restructuring to address North American competitiveness.

items.title: Here's Why You Should Retain DaVita Stock in Your Portfolio for Now
items.summary: DaVita (DVA) has rallied 55.8% year-to-date, driven by strong Integrated Kidney Care (IKC) platform growth, improving treatment volumes, and technology investments. The company beat Q2 expectations by $40 million in adjusted operating income and raised full-year guidance. However, persistent headwinds include declining revenue per treatment due to commercial-mix pressure (estimated $70 million impact in 2027), elevated G&A costs limiting operating leverage, and limited acquisition opportunities in a consolidated market.

items.title: ONTO's $1.1 Billion Backlog: Can Growth Accelerate Into 2027?
items.summary: Onto Innovation (ONTO) is experiencing significant growth driven by AI infrastructure spending, with backlog more than doubling to $1.1B in Q2 2026. The company raised full-year revenue guidance and expects 80% growth in advanced packaging. However, it faces intensifying competition from larger rivals KLA and Applied Materials, who are also benefiting from the semiconductor equipment boom.

items.title: Here's What $10,000 Invested in JPMorgan Chase When Jamie Dimon Became CEO Is Worth Now
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase stock has significantly outperformed the S&P 500 under CEO Jamie Dimon's 20+ year tenure. A $10,000 investment made when Dimon became CEO in 2006 would be worth approximately $83,020 today (730% gain), compared to $62,420 for the S&P 500 (524% gain). Including dividends, JPMorgan's total return reaches 1,320%, turning the initial investment into $141,540. Dimon plans to remain CEO for several more years.

items.title: Can Rising IRST Demand Support Boeing's Defense Growth Outlook?
items.summary: Boeing secured a $42.2 million contract to produce IRST Block II sensor assemblies for the U.S. Navy and Royal Australian Air Force. The company is well-positioned to benefit from growing military demand for advanced infrared sensing technologies that provide passive detection capabilities. However, Boeing's stock carries a Sell rating with declining earnings estimates and trades at a discount to industry peers.

items.title: Prediction: 2 Stocks That Will Be Worth More Than Broadcom 5 Years From Now
items.summary: The article predicts that Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Palantir Technologies will surpass Broadcom's $1.7 trillion valuation within five years. AMD needs approximately 70% growth, supported by its major OpenAI deal for GPU capacity. Palantir would need to roughly quadruple from its current $456 billion valuation, driven by exceptional commercial revenue growth of 149% year-over-year. Both stocks carry execution risks but are positioned to benefit from AI market expansion.

items.title: AI Crawlers Turned Away More Than Twice as Often, a Check to Run Before an AI Visibility Audit
items.summary: Zen Media released guidance on AI visibility audits for brands that rank on Google but go unnamed in AI answers. Data shows AI crawler access denials increased to 13.47% in Q3 2026, with search and user-triggered AI requests growing from 6.51% to 11.92% between Q2 and Q3. The company's audit measures brand visibility across Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok, identifying gaps between SEO performance and AI answer inclusion.

items.title: Top Storage Stock to Buy With $500 Right Now
items.summary: Everpure (formerly Pure Storage) is recommended as a top storage stock pick, with AI-driven demand accelerating revenue growth to 38% year-over-year. The company's software-based flash storage approach delivers superior price performance, and a recent hyperscaler deal is expected to generate significant revenue from fiscal 2028 onward. Trading at a reasonable 1.16x PEG multiple, the stock carries volatility risk from potential flash price reversals.

items.title: If You're Worried About an AI Bubble, Here's the Tech Stock Portfolio I'd Build
items.summary: Despite concerns about an AI bubble with some stocks trading at extreme valuations, the article identifies three major tech companies as relatively safe AI investments: Nvidia with a P/E of 31 and strong revenue growth, Amazon leveraging AI through AWS with stable e-commerce backing, and Alphabet benefiting from AI in advertising and cloud services. All three maintain strong liquidity and profitability despite significant capital expenditure commitments.

items.title: Taiwan Construction Market Size, Trends, and Forecasts by Sector to 2030 (H1 2026) | AI, Semiconductor Plants, Renewables, and Transport Drive 3.9% Annual Growth
items.summary: Taiwan's construction industry is forecast to expand 3.6% in 2026 and average 3.9% annual growth through 2030, driven by investments in semiconductor manufacturing, AI infrastructure, renewable energy, and transport networks. items.title: Here's Where Palantir and 4 Other AI Software Stocks Could Be in 5 Years
items.summary: The article analyzes five AI software stocks divided into two camps: those proving AI revenue (Palantir, CrowdStrike) trading at steep valuations with limited room for error, and those offering faster growth at lower multiples (SoundHound, AppLovin, ServiceNow). Each company presents different risk-reward profiles over the next five years, with concerns ranging from valuation sustainability to market dependency.

items.title: Michael Burry Is Betting Against Artificial Intelligence (AI). Here's the Case for and Against, and the One Stock I'd Still Own.
items.summary: Michael Burry has increased his bearish bets against AI stocks, warning of a potential crash.
